content:
The Volume (Capacity) chapter is a dependable source of marks in the CTET Paper I (Classes I–V) Mathematics section — and it is one you can master quickly with the right practice. This guide explains what CTET volume capacity actually tests, the facts and formulas worth memorising, the mistakes that quietly cost marks, and a free 10-question online test you can take right now to check where you stand.

Work through the quiz below first, read the explanation for anything you miss, then use the chapter-test e-book at the end for full, exam-style practice. That "test → review → practise" loop is how serious CTET candidates turn a weak topic into a strong one.

What Volume (Capacity) covers in CTET Paper I Maths

At the primary level this chapter blends content knowledge with pedagogy — how young children learn the idea. Expect questions on:

  • The idea of capacity — how much a container holds
  • Litres and millilitres
  • Converting between L and mL
  • Measuring and comparing liquids

Practise the full syllabus free on the CTET Paper I Mathematics course at vidaara.org, then test yourself here.

Key facts and formulas to remember

  • 1 litre = 1000 millilitres.
  • To change L to mL multiply by 1000; mL to L divide by 1000.
  • A spoon holds about 5 mL; a water bottle about 1 L.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Confusing capacity (litres) with mass (kilograms).
  • Forgetting 1 L = 1000 mL in conversions.

quiz.title: CTET Volume (Capacity) Practice Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten CTET Paper I – pattern questions on Volume (Capacity). Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: A recipe requires 250 mL of milk. If you want to make the recipe 3 times, how many litres of milk are needed in total?
questions.explanation: Total milk = 250 mL × 3 = 750 mL. Since 1 L = 1000 mL, 750 mL = 750 / 1000 = 0.75 L. This integrates the conversion concept into a real-life scenario.

questions.q: A bucket has a capacity of 12 liters. How many full 250 mL mugs of water are needed to fill the bucket completely?
questions.explanation: Capacity of bucket = 12 L = 12,000 mL. Capacity of one mug = 250 mL. Number of mugs needed = 12,000 / 250 = 48 mugs.

questions.q: A jar holds 2 L 400 mL of fruit syrup. If 8 identical small glass bottles are filled completely from this jar, what is the capacity of each small bottle?
questions.explanation: Total syrup volume = 2 L 400 mL = 2400 mL. Number of bottles = 8. Capacity of one bottle = 2400 / 8 = 300 mL.

questions.q: A water container is three-fourths full and holds 15 liters of water. What is the total capacity of the container in milliliters?
questions.explanation: Let total capacity be C liters. (3/4) × C = 15 L C = 15 × (4/3) = 20 L. Converting to mL: 20 × 1000 = 20,000 mL.

questions.q: An oil tin contains 15 Litres of oil. A cook uses 1 L 250 mL on Monday, 2 L 500 mL on Tuesday, and 1 L 750 mL on Wednesday. How much oil remains in the tin?
questions.explanation: 1. Total oil used = 1250 mL + 2500 mL + 1750 mL = 5500 mL = 5 L 500 mL. 2. Oil remaining = 15 L - 5 L 500 mL = 14 L 1000 mL - 5 L 500 mL = 9 L 500 mL.

questions.q: Which of the following liquid quantities is best measured in Liters rather than Milliliters?
options: The dosage of an eye drop
Ink inside a fountain pen cartridge
Perfume inside a pocket spray bottle
questions.explanation: Large volumes of liquids like water in swimming pools, overhead tanks, or ponds are measured using Liters (L) or larger units, whereas small quantities like drops, ink cartridges, and sprays are measured in Milliliters (mL).

questions.q: Which of the following daily life items would be measured using milliliters (mL) rather than Litres (L)?
options: Water stored in a municipal storage tank
Fuel stored in a petrol tanker lorry
Ink capacity of a fountain pen converter
Water filled in a household bathing tub
questions.explanation: Fountain pen converters hold very minute quantities of liquid (usually under 2 mL), making milliliters the appropriate unit. Municipal tanks, tankers, and bathtubs involve large volumes measured in Litres.

questions.q: Which of the following is the most reasonable estimation for the capacity of a standard box carton of milk bought at a retail grocery counter?
questions.explanation: A typical retail milk carton or pouch holds around 500 mL to 1 Litre. 1 mL is just a few drops, while 100 L and 500 L are industrial quantities.

questions.q: How many millilitres are there in 4 Litres and 500 millilitres?
questions.explanation: 1 Litre = 1000 mL, so 4 Litres = 4 × 1000 = 4000 mL. Total = 4000 mL + 500 mL = 4500 mL.

questions.q: A container holds 3 Litres of soup. If each bowl holds 250 mL of soup, how many bowls can be filled completely from the container?
questions.explanation: Total volume = 3 L = 3000 mL. Capacity of one bowl = 250 mL. Number of bowls = 3000 ÷ 250 = 12 bowls.

faq.q: How many millilitres are in a litre?

faq.a: Capacity is the amount of liquid a container can hold, measured in litres (L) and millilitres (mL).
